engineCode: replay/fill/statistics copied from /home/team/shared/backtest/run_backtest.ts — differences listed in differencesFromH1Run
differencesFromH1Run: data granularity D (daily) and data dir /home/team/shared/daily/data instead of H1 /home/team/shared/backtest/data
gap accounting: weekdays with no bar inside the span (daily FX has no weekend bars), not an hourly grid
holding time reported in days (plus hours and bar count); day-bucketed histogram
no reconciliation against the live dashboard, which is an H1 engine — a daily trigger is not comparable to an H1 signal
H1 headline figures embedded for comparison by reading /home/team/shared/backtest/results.json

EUR_USD.label: EUR/USD
EUR_USD.gapRule: each bar is shifted +3h onto its trading day before the weekday check (daily bars are stamped at the 21:00/22:00 UTC rollover, so a Sunday-stamped bar is Monday's session); a weekday with no bar is a missing trading day
EUR_USD.spreadTimingNote: the bar opens at the daily rollover, which is also the moment of the day when spreads are widest — so a fill at the next bar's open pays a wider-than-average spread for the pair

measurementPeriod.note: The ruleset cannot produce a first event before bar index 200 (EMA(200)); the measurement period is therefore the full cached span minus that warm-up (~10 months of daily bars).

assumptions.fillHeadline: entry at the NEXT bar's open, ASK for a long / BID for a short; exits at the opposite side. No look-ahead.
assumptions.fillOptimistic: entry at the trigger bar's CLOSE (mid), exits at the exit bar's close (mid) — labelled OPTIMISTIC UPPER BOUND, not achievable.
assumptions.fillZeroCost: same timing as headline (next-bar open) but at MID on both sides, so the spread drag is visible.
assumptions.intraBarAmbiguity: if a bar touches both stop and target, the STOP is counted first.
assumptions.gaps: a bar opening beyond the stop fills at that bar's open (worse than the stop); a bar opening beyond the target fills at that bar's open (better than the target).
assumptions.ruleExit: an exit the rules trigger at a bar's close is filled at the NEXT bar's open, same no-look-ahead rule as entries.
assumptions.stopsAndTargets: stop = 1.5 x ATR(14) and target = 3.0 x ATR(14), both measured from the trigger bar's mid close, identical to the live engine. Stop/target are treated as exit triggers alongside the rule's own exit (cross against, or trend-filter flip).
assumptions.optimisation: NONE. No parameter search, no sweep, no per-pair tuning. One ruleset, unchanged from the H1 run.
assumptions.r: 1R = the trade's initial stop distance (1.5 x ATR(14) at the trigger bar, in pips).
assumptions.spreadSource: the ASK minus BID of the same bar in the owner's own OANDA practice-account history — a real historical spread per bar, not an assumption.

exclusions: swap / financing / carry charges — NOT modelled
slippage beyond the quoted bid/ask spread — NOT modelled
commission, fees and taxes — NOT modelled
position sizing and account equity — NOT modelled; every result is in pips and R
weekend/holiday gaps are left as gaps; no bar is interpolated or filled in

reconciliationWithLive.why: the live dashboard runs the ruleset on H1 bars; a daily trigger bar cannot be compared to an H1 signal, so this check is not meaningful and is not claimed as passed.

combinedHeadline.note: Holding time is what decides how much of a trade's cost is swap/financing. Swap is NOT modelled anywhere in this run — these figures exist only to size that omission, and they say it is large: at a daily median hold a trade pays multiple rollovers.

inR.note: spread paid as a fraction of the trade's initial risk (1R = 1.5 x ATR(14)). This is the number that decides whether lower frequency improved the cost-to-edge ratio.

costEdgeDecomposition.howComputed: spreadPaid = zero-cost expectancy (mid fills, same timing) minus headline expectancy (next-bar open at ask/bid). Both from the stored results; nothing typed by hand. The zero-cost replay fills at mid and can exit on a mid high/low rather than a bid/ask one, so a handful of trades may exit on a different bar; the subtraction is therefore a whole-book cost measure, not a per-trade ledger.

crossCheck.note: one full spread per round trip (enter at ask / exit at bid, or the reverse) should equal the spread-paid figure above if the two runs took the same trades

optimisticUpperBound_triggerClose.label: OPTIMISTIC UPPER BOUND — fills at the trigger bar's close, which is only knowable after that bar has ended. NOT achievable in practice.

headline.note: a year counts as positive if the combined headline pips for trades CLOSED in that year are above zero
